text:
maria.g: Hi folks — I'm traveling to Spain from May 10–28 and my OB wants to do a transabdominal ultrasound while I'm there (routine check, not emergency). I haven't received my new ID card yet. Can benefits help with pre-authorization or a letter so the clinic can bill Aetna directly instead of me paying upfront?
sasha.peoples: Hey Maria — we can help. Quick Q: is the provider asking to bill Aetna directly, or are they saying you must pay and submit for reimbursement?
maria.g: They said they'd prefer to bill directly but asked for an authorization/reference from the insurer. Clinic requested member ID and a "direct bill" confirmation. I only have the plan name (Redwood Core PPO) and last 4 of member ID — I don't have the physical card.
ben.benefits: Tagging benefits team — we can request a direct-bill confirmation/authorization. We usually need the full member ID and DOB. If you don't have the full ID we can pull the member number from our vendor portal and generate a letter.
luis.hr: If it's routine and not urgent we should be able to get a pre-trip verification. Ben — what's the typical SLA for this?
ben.benefits: SLA is ~2 business days for a standard pre-auth/guarantee letter if we have all info. If vendor needs extra clinical notes it can take longer. We can start today.
aetna-bot: [auto] Created case AET-84219 for direct-billing request. Please provide the following: member full name, DOB, full member ID (or SS# last4), provider name + address, expected service date, CPT/description.
maria.g: Thanks — posting the details now. Member: Maria Gomez / DOB 1992-04-14 / Member ID last4: 6789. Provider: Centro Imagen Mama / Calle Mayor 12, Madrid. Expected service date: 2028-05-15. CPT: pelvic ultrasound 76856 (OB follow-up). Clinic contact: Dr. Alvarez, +34 91 555 0101.
ben.benefits: Perfect. I'm attaching required info to the ticket and requesting a "letter of direct billing" + a pre-authorization number. Also including guidance for the clinic on claim submission.
sasha.peoples: Maria — while vendor processes this, take a photo of the clinic's billing page and the estimate. If they insist on upfront payment, save receipt copies — we'll help submit for expedited reimbursement.
maria.g: Got it. Clinic said they can do direct billing if they get the auth# and plan ID. Sending screenshot: https://files.redwood.example/IMG_20280512.jpg
ben.benefits: Received. Aetna says they may require diagnosis code instead of CPT in some markets. Suggested ICD-10: O09.2 or Z36 depending on note. If possible ask clinic to include the ICD-10 on the claim.
aetna-bot: [auto] Update: Case AET-84219 updated. Preliminary pre-auth number: PA-2028-05-0097 (pending final review). Letter of Direct Billing will be emailed to member and clinic on record within 24–48 hours.
luis.hr: For travel records, also file in HRA/benefits portal under "international care" so we have a company-side copy in case of ad-hoc escalation.
maria.g: Appreciate it — should I forward the clinic's invoice back here if they bill me?
ben.benefits: Yes — if you end up paying, scan the invoice + proof of payment and we'll start expedited reimbursement. Reimbursement timelines vary but we will push for priority due to travel.
sasha.peoples: Quick checklist for the clinic to ensure direct billing works:```
- Use member ID or plan name exactly: "Redwood Core PPO"
- Include ICD-10 and CPT codes (e.g., CPT 76856)
- Send claim to Aetna international claims unit: intclaims@aetna.com or via vendor portal
- Reference pre-auth PA-2028-05-0097 in claim notes
- Include clinic NPI/tax ID or local equivalent
```
ben.benefits: Also note some Spanish clinics use local billing codes; if that happens Aetna may ask for an itemized invoice mapping to US CPTs. Keep an itemized receipt.
aetna-bot: [auto] Final: Letter of Direct Billing attached to case AET-84219 and emailed to member and clinic at 2028-05-13T14:02Z. Please confirm receipt.
maria.g: I received the email and the clinic confirmed they got the letter. Thank you all!! :tada:
sasha.peoples: Great — marking as resolved in our tracker but leave the thread open if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
